\[
T_v=\inf\{k\ge0:X_k=v\},
\]

\[
\tau(G)=\max_{u,v\in V(G)}\bigl(\mathbb E_uT_v+\mathbb E_vT_u\bigr),
\qquad
 t_n=\max_{G\in\mathcal R_n}\tau(G).
\]

72	## Proof
73	
74	### 1. The determinant tests and their bounds
75	
76	The numbers \(b_{ij}(a)\) are precisely the successive binary digits of \(a\). Consequently, as \(a\) ranges from \(0\) to \(2^m-1\), these arrays run through every symmetric zero-diagonal \(0\)-\(1\) array exactly once.
77	
78	For the proof, interpret one such array as the adjacency matrix of a graph. Its Laplacian is \(L_a\). For every real vector \(x\),
79	\[
80	x^{\mathsf T}L_a x
81	=\sum_{\{i,j\}:\,b_{ij}(a)=1}(x_i-x_j)^2.
82	\tag{2}
83	\]
84	In particular, \(L_a\) and all its principal submatrices are positive semidefinite.
85	
86	Consider \(A=(L_a)_{\widehat{\{1\}}}\). Extend a vector indexed by \(V\setminus\{1\}\) by putting its coordinate at \(1\) equal to zero. Equation (2) shows that \(A\) is positive definite exactly when the graph is connected:
87	
88	* In a connected graph, zero energy forces all coordinates to be equal, hence zero.
89	* In a disconnected graph, the indicator of a component not containing \(1\) gives a nonzero zero-energy vector.
90	
91	Thus
92	\[
93	D_a>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{the graph is connected}.
94	\tag{3}
95	\]
96	Also \(D_a\) is a nonnegative integer. Hadamard’s determinant inequality gives
97	\[
98	0\le D_a
99	\le \prod_{i\ne1}d_i(a)
100	\le(n-1)^{n-1}=H.
101	\tag{4}
102	\]
103	Positive semidefiniteness also gives \(F_a\ge0\).
104	
105	It follows immediately that
106	\[
107	c_a=
108	\begin{cases}
109	1,&\text{the graph is connected},\\
110	0,&\text{otherwise}.
111	\end{cases}
112	\tag{5}
113	\]
114	Likewise, since the degrees are integers,
115	\[
116	r_a=
117	\begin{cases}
118	1,&d_0(a)=d_1(a)=\cdots=d_{n-1}(a),\\
119	0,&\text{otherwise}.
120	\end{cases}
121	\tag{6}
122	\]
123	
124	In particular, \(D_a+1-c_a\) equals \(D_a\) in the connected case and \(1\) otherwise, so it is always positive.

126	### 2. An exact determinant formula for the commute time
127	
128	Let \(G\) be connected and \(d\)-regular, with Laplacian \(L\). For a vertex \(v\), let
129	\[
130	h^{(v)}_i=\mathbb E_iT_v.
131	\]
132	These expectations are finite: from every vertex there is a path of at most \(n-1\) steps to \(v\), and connectedness gives a uniform positive probability of following such a path in any block of \(n-1\) steps.
133	
134	The first-step equations say
135	\[
136	h^{(v)}_i=1+\frac1d\sum_{j\sim i}h^{(v)}_j

138	\]

192	\]
